```{r, include = FALSE}
has_deps <- requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("crosstalk", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("DT", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.align = "center",
  eval = has_deps
)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = !has_deps, results = "asis"}
cat("This vignette needs the plotly, crosstalk and DT packages. ",
    "Install them with install.packages(c(\"plotly\", \"crosstalk\", \"DT\")).", sep = "")
```

The interactive plots are for exploring the data.
Hover over a peptide to see its sequence, uptake, difference and p-value.
Plots built together are linked: a peptide selected in one is highlighted in all of them.
For figures in a paper, use the static plots (`plot_fissure_vent()`, `plots_vol_tp()`).

The plots need the plotly, crosstalk and DT packages.
They are optional and are not installed with HDXBoxeR.

| Function | Shows |
|---|---|
| `interactive_volcano()` | volcano plot |
| `interactive_fissure_vent()` | fissure vent plot (`vignette("fissure_vent")`) |
| `interactive_woods()` | Woods plot |
| `significant_peptides_table()` | table of all peptides |
| `interactive_fissure_explorer()` | all four together, linked |

The significance test is the same as in the rest of the package.

## Example

```{r}
library(HDXBoxeR)
file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
a <- output_tp(file_nm)
```

One plot:

```{r}
interactive_fissure_vent(a, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound", times = "1800.00s")
```

Give several `alpha` and `pvalue` values to switch between them with a dropdown (top right):

```{r}
interactive_fissure_vent(a, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound", times = "1800.00s",
                         alpha = c(0.01, 0.05), pvalue = c(0.01, 0.05))
```

`alpha` and `pvalue` are paired: the first with the first, the second with the second.

All plots together.
Select rows in the table, or hover over a peptide, to highlight it everywhere:

```{r fig.height = 9}
interactive_fissure_explorer(a, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound", times = "1800.00s")
```

## Saving

Save one plot with `htmlwidgets::saveWidget()`.
The explorer is a layout of several plots, so save it with `htmltools::save_html()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
explorer <- interactive_fissure_explorer(a, state1 = "Unbound", state2 = "bound", times = "1800.00s")
htmltools::save_html(explorer, "fissure_explorer.html")
```

The saved file opens in any browser, without R.

## Good to know

-   One time point per call.
-   `p_adjust = "BH"` corrects the p-values for multiple testing.

## How this connects to the rest of the package

| Interactive | Static version | Explained in |
|---|---|---|
| `interactive_volcano()` | `plots_vol_tp()` | `vignette("HDXBoxeR")` |
| `interactive_fissure_vent()` | `plot_fissure_vent()` | `vignette("fissure_vent")` |
| `interactive_woods()` | `woods_CI_plot()` | `vignette("HDXBoxeR")` |
| `significant_peptides_table()` | `hdx_results_table()`, `diff_peptides_prep()` | `vignette("HDXBoxeR")` |

To show results on a structure, see `vignette("hdx_structure")`.
